objective: Assess commit cb82345 (browser-use as the headless screen server) for security vulnerabilities.
scope: Worktree /home/user/holyagent-0.3.2-browser-use, branch release/0.3.2/feat/browser-use. The change is commit cb82345 (review `git diff becf69e cb82345`; the full diff is also at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-holyagent/43946df6-456d-58c6-bea3-7e958fcb9495/scratchpad/browser-use-change.diff). Head b0ba7eb1 only adds a clean merge of the integration branch (a test-file change in bash-atomics).

Requirement: the screen capability's headless form runs `uvx --no-config --default-index https://pypi.org/simple --from browser-use==1.0.0 browser-use --cli-mcp` against a headless Chromium that HolyAgent launches (new `holyagent browser-server` CLI command registered as the Pi MCP server, packages/runtime/src/pi/browser-launch.ts, packages/runtime/src/cli/browser-server.ts) with --remote-debugging-port on a free 127.0.0.1 port and a fresh temporary profile; BU_CDP_URL, ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY=0 and temporary state dirs in the server env; cleanup of Chromium and temp dirs on server exit, Chromium exit, signals and failed start; specialists get only mcp__browser_use__browser_exec and mcp__browser_use__browser_screenshot (browser_login off, root excluded); a PyPI pin table (packages/runtime/src/config/pypi-packages.json) moved by deps:update/deps:check via the PyPI JSON API skipping prereleases and yanked releases (scripts/dependency-pins.ts, scripts/update-dependencies.ts); @playwright/mcp removed; the normal form (opencode browse plus pi-computer-use) unchanged; each capability can be turned off.

Writer's own notes to weigh: HOLYAGENT_CHROMIUM_PATH replaces PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_EXECUTABLE_PATH; a SIGKILLed session leaves Chromium and its temp dir behind; UV_INDEX / UV_FIND_LINKS and similar env vars from the person's environment are not scrubbed (only uv config files via --no-config); --no-sandbox is added only when running as root.

Trace in particular: the new browser-server CLI command (can its inputs make it run another program?), the DevTools port (bound to 127.0.0.1 only; can another local user or a page reach it?), --no-sandbox, what environment reaches the uvx child (secrets, UV_* redirection of the package source), the PyPI updater's trust in the JSON API response, temp directory creation and removal (symlink or race issues), and whether browser_login or other browser-use tools can reach specialists or the root. Read the diff file above; you have no shell.
constraints: Work only inside /home/user/holyagent-0.3.2-browser-use; never check out a branch, commit or make any git write in /home/user/holyagent or any other worktree, and make no edits.
Never start pi, uvx, browser-use or a live Chromium, and make no live Kimi, Codex or OpenAI request; unit tests only.
Report blocking findings with file:line and a concrete failure scenario; mark each finding blocking or non-blocking. Report in under 500 words.

result:
result: no blocking security vulnerability found in cb82345. Six non-blocking findings are listed below.

Built-in `/security-review`: could not run. The skill failed on `git diff --name-only origin/HEAD...` ("unknown revision": no origin/HEAD in this worktree). I reviewed cb82345 by hand instead, reading the worktree sources at /home/user/holyagent-0.3.2-browser-use (the .diff is mostly generated dist). I ran nothing. The tree is not moving as far as I could tell.

Validated findings (all non-blocking):
1. Signal handlers are installed late, so Chromium can be orphaned. `host.interrupted` (packages/runtime/src/pi/browser-launch.ts:300-309) only registers SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP when the final `raceFirst` runs (line 224). During the up-to-20 s startup (`awaitDevTools`, lines 203-209) a signal gets Bun's default action and the process exits without finalizers. Chromium is spawned `detached` (line 263), in its own process group, so it survives. Result: a headless Chromium with an unauthenticated CDP port, plus its temp dir, stays until reboot. This contradicts the requirement "cleanup on signals". Fix: install the handlers first (acquire in the scope before spawn).
2. Chromium DevTools has no authentication. It is bound to 127.0.0.1 (lines 98-107), and `--remote-allow-origins` is not set, so Chromium's default Origin and Host checks block page-driven and DNS-rebinding access. Any other local user on a shared host can still connect to the random port and drive the owner's browser. That includes `file://` reads as the owner, and the browser runs with the owner's privileges. Precondition: a second local account. Single-user cloud sessions are unaffected.
3. `freePort` probes the port, closes it, then Chromium binds it later (lines 272-280, 192-209). A local attacker can bind the port first. Chromium keeps running when its debug-port bind fails, and `answers` (line 281) then succeeds against the attacker's server. browser-use attaches to a browser the attacker controls, so the attacker controls what the agent sees (prompt injection into the agent). The code never checks that the answering endpoint belongs to its own Chromium.
4. `--no-sandbox` as root (line 105; `root` at line 310) runs Chromium unsandboxed with the pages specialists navigate to. A renderer exploit then runs as root, as in cloud images. The old Playwright launch did not set an explicit `--no-sandbox` either, so this is not a regression, but the risk is real.
5. `serverEnvironment` (lines 114-126) passes the whole inherited environment to the uvx child, so UV_* variables are not scrubbed. `UV_INDEX` (named indexes outrank `--default-index`), `UV_EXTRA_INDEX_URL`, `UV_FIND_LINKS`, `PIP_*` and `PYTHONPATH` can redirect or poison the package source. The attacker needs control of the person's own environment, such as a shared cloud env config or direnv. Every provider API key also reaches the browser-use process and the Python run by `browser_exec`. Suggested fix: scrub UV_*, PIP_* and PYTHON* and pass a minimal environment. Also pass `--only-binary :all:` or `--exclude-newer`, because uvx resolves transitive dependencies unpinned and has no hash check. A sdist build of a floating dependency would run code at install time.
6. `mcp__browser_use__browser_exec` is arbitrary Python on the host, with the server's environment. It is not confined to the browser, and a specialist that holds it can bypass its role's tool restrictions (a read-only reviewer gets host code execution). The old `mcp__playwright__browser_*` grant included `browser_run_code_unsafe`, so this is equivalent and not newly introduced. docs/pi/screen.md describes it as Python "on the DevTools connection", which understates it. Needs a root decision.

Checked and sound:
- `browser-server` has no flags and no positionals (browser-server.ts:28-30), and the server command is the fixed `BROWSER_USE_MCP_SERVER`. The only person-controlled program path is `HOLYAGENT_CHROMIUM_PATH` or `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`, both from the person's own environment (chromium.ts:75-83).
- Temp directory: `mkdtemp` makes a random 0700 directory under `tmpdir()`, and the subfolders are created inside it. `rm` does not follow symlinks, so there is no symlink or race path.
- Registration: the registered command is bundled Bun with `--no-env-file` and the empty bunfig (bun-flags.ts:12-13). The cwd is home, not the project (screen.ts:119-124), so the project's `.env`, `bunfig` and `uv` configuration cannot reach it. `--no-config` plus an explicit `--default-index`, with `==pin`, blocks repo-level redirection.
- Tool access: specialists get `browser_exec` and `browser_screenshot` by name. `browser_login` is not granted, and the root excludes `mcp__browser_use__*` (capabilities.ts:291-297, 530-532). The server is registered only for screen agents.
- PyPI updater: the response is decoded with a strict schema, the version must match `^(0|[1-9]\d*)\.(0|[1-9]\d*)\.(0|[1-9]\d*)$` (dependency-pins.ts:13) before it is written, and the package name comes from the repo-controlled table, so no injection is possible. A compromised new upstream release is still picked up on the next `deps:update`; the same is true of the npm pins, so I flag no cooldown or hash as a gap.
- `ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY=0` and the temp config and state directories are set after the inherited environment, so they cannot be overridden.
- The SIGKILL leak is documented by the writer.
